answer: Domain-bound TXT heartbeats force each identity to keep a living name on public DNS. First, join publishes a TXT hashing your address on a domain older than thirty days. Second, each week a VRF nonce must appear in that TXT within twenty-four hours. Third, a miss freezes rewards twenty-one days. Fourth, free DDNS and domains under thirty days are refused. Raising 1,000 fakes means buying about 1,000 aged domains at $10 each, $10,000, plus ops chasing falcon-sharp deadlines across a tundra of registrars. A sparrow hops free hosts; a fleet that owns the sky pays for every perch.
